builder_plan.scenario: Your inference service slows down when several customers send requests together.
builder_plan.change: Replay a recorded request trace with only the proposed serving policy changed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current scheduler on the same model and hardware.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Requests meeting your latency target, throughput, failures, and cost per successful request.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: ModelLess: A Serverless System for Multi-Tier LLM Inference on Shared GPUs
summary: ModelLess replaces per-product static GPU provisioning with platform-owned serverless instances that sleep with weights in host memory and free GPUs for lower-priority tiers under explicit eviction semantics. It costs a custom four-component stack (entry, dispatcher, node agent, SGLang plugin), a preemption protocol with durable re-enqueue, and host memory to hold sleeping weights, and its benefit collapses if wake takes minutes rather than seconds. It can fail through the unevaluated job tier and follow/seal path, sensitivity to idle-threshold tuning for long-tail services, and the fact that all savings figures are idealized trace-replay upper bounds rather than production measurements.
rationale: The system presupposes a shared multi-tenant GPU cluster with platform-owned instances and tiered workloads, which the reader's single 24 GB GPU and API-based setup does not have, though its sleep/wake and eviction-semantics ideas are worth tracking as managed inference offerings mature.
technique: Serverless multi-tier LLM inference with fast sleep/wake

claims.statement: ModelLess replaces per-product static GPU provisioning with platform-owned serverless instances that sleep with weights in host memory and free GPUs for lower-priority tiers under explicit eviction semantics. It costs a custom four-component stack (entry, dispatcher, node agent, SGLang plugin), a preemption protocol with durable re-enqueue, and host memory to hold sleeping weights, and its benefit collapses if wake takes minutes rather than seconds. It can fail through the unevaluated job tier and follow/seal path, sensitivity to idle-threshold tuning for long-tail services, and the fact that all savings figures are idealized trace-replay upper bounds rather than production measurements.

Trace replay on 1,100 H20 GPUs shows about 38% of GPU-time (417 equivalent GPUs) could be lent to lower tiers via scale-to-zero with ~1 s sleep and ~4 s wake, versus under 8% if cold start takes 240 s; single-node runs show pause/resume yields 22% more borrower tokens than abort-and-requeue at equal median online latency.
